It's been a memorable game, thank you for keeping me company through it with your 
emails. I hope you enjoyed following it on Cricinfo as much as I did bringing it to you. 
Until the next one, goodnight! 
Chahal: "I think it was a team effort, we wanted to stay positive, take 2-3 wickets in the 
powerplay, pitch wasnt easy. There was turn in the pitch as well. My first ball turned, so 
Shreyas said let's have a slip, we needed to take wickets to win this game because the 
runs were low. I always had self belief in myself. I always think about how to get the 
batters out, I varied my pace so that the batters had to put effort into hitting." 
Chahal is the Player of the Match of course for 4-0-28-4. 
Shreyas Iyer at the presentation: "It's had to express in words, I saw the ball was turning 
a bit, asked Yuzi to control his breathing as much as possible, we needed to be 
attacking, I'm not able to talk, it's tough to digest this victory ... When I went out to bat i 
faced two balls, one stayed low, the other carried, there was variable bounce in the 
wicket ... we got to a decent total, considering we won by 16 runs ... the bounce wasn't 
consistent and the pace was variable ... Two wickets in two overs gave us momentum 
but their two batters took the momentum towards them, but when Yuzi started turning 
the ball, our expectations and hopes got higher, I wanted the fielders to be attacking 
around the batsmen so that they try different shots, and the tide turned towards us. We 
need to stay humble ...this win is going to give us a boost." 
Akshay: "Wonder how Varun judged this as a 180-190 wicket during the innings break!" 
Mustafa Moudi : "So Chahal saved himself for this match. Last match Dhoni and tonight 
Chahal, once again proved - FORM IS TEMPORARY, CLASS IS PERMANENT!!" 
If Ponting is saying that it's the best game he's been part of as coach, that's got to count 
for a whole lot. Stay tuned for the presentation. 
Ricky Ponting: The heart rate is still up there ... two days agp we couldn't chase 240 off 
... small chases like this, the wicket was easy. How about Chahal tonight? He actually 
had a fitness test beforee the game tonight ... I asked him if he was okay, he said he 
was ready to go ... even if we had lost that game, I couldnt have been prouder of us in 
the second half, the batting was poor, but ... if we had gone down in a close one, I 
thought this was a season defining moment. I reckon at the half way mark there weren't 
too many people around the world who would have defended that ... That might just be 
about the best win I've ever had as coach." 
I have almost never heard Ajinkya Rahane express himself in the manner he has just 
now. 
Rahane: "I'll take the blame, played the wrong shot, was missing, but it started from 
there. I didn't want to take a chance at the time, I wasn't sure as well. wicket was not 
that easy, 111 was chaseable, we batted really badly as a batting unit, bowlers did really 
well against a strong Punjab batting line up. I thought we were reckless, should take full 
responsibility as a unit. Too many things going through my head. Very disappointed. 
Need to keep myself really calm and think about what I'm going to talk to the boys." 
Punjab's players are still hugging it out in the middle. What a turnaround for Chahal, 
what a night for Shreyas Iyer after his second-ball duck. We were talking about KKR 
going No. 1 on NRR an hour ago. Just incredible scenes.
